messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_t\) be the length of the red stick after \(t\) minutes, with \(L_0=1\).

Before the \(t\)-th break, he has exactly \(t\) sticks, and exactly one of them has the red endpoint. So the red stick is chosen with probability

\[
\frac{1}{t}.
\]

If it is chosen, its length is halved; otherwise its length stays the same. Thus

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_t \mid \text{previous history}]
=
\left(1-\frac1t\right)L_{t-1}+\frac1t\cdot \frac{L_{t-1}}2
=
\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)L_{t-1}.
\]

Taking expectations,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_t]=\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)\mathbb{E}[L_{t-1}].
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\prod_{t=1}^5 \left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)
=
\frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}.
\]

So

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 9}{2\cdot 4\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot 10}
=
\frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
